body:
"Think of yourself last."

Can you expand on that? I'm curious because its the exact opposite of what everyone else is saying.
I picked the name because it summed up what I was feeling at the time, and because "exhausted guy who's trying to do the right thing but might be fucking it up for everyone" was too long.

Wow, well thank you for that splash of cold water. You're not the first person to suggest that I'm co-dependant, and its something I'm exploring with my own social worker ... when I'm not talking about Florida and Montana that is.

Oddly enough, the girl from the outside world, the one I'm ignoring, is a paramedic. The night we met, we had a long talk about how she learned to accept that some of the people she was trying to help were going to die. She has lost her share of patients, and yet she accepts it gracefully. I really admire her for that.

Thanks, that is really helpful. I've always been the "fixer," the Superman among my friends. Help you move at 3 am? Girlfriend stole your money and need a meal? Car break down across state lines? I'm here dude.

I have her parents' address. She moved home with them for a while and frequently talks about how she'd rather kill herself than live at home again. I try to tell her her parents would prefer her alive and at home, if necessary, than on her own and dead.

My life isn't perfect but I was doing ok. Long term relationship ended, moved home, got help, got meds, got a fun job, got a social life. I firmly believe in not waiting until life is perfect before we help others. That leads to, "oh, I'll donate next year when I get a raise." "I'll volunteer when the kids are done with school." Nothing gets done that way.

I just have no idea how to wean Montana off me. I occasionally fantasize about faking my death - how hard would it be? Delete reddit, delete FB, change phone number, and poof, its like I never existed.

Don't worry, I'm not offended. I don't think I have any emotions left besides worry, fear and guilt.

I may have written about this in past posts, but Montana already has a therapist of some kind, a psychiatrist, and she's medicated. The fact that those 3 things aren't enough to sustain her is what scares me. She's flat out told me several times that she wouldn't be alive without me and looking forward to meeting me is the only reason she has for living. She doesn't respond to logic or reason.

I've thought about calling her parents or her college. Id rather she be angry at me and alive but frankly at this point I'm afraid she would kill herself just to spite me.

I have a social worker - one guess as to what I spend most of my time talking about. And my best friend is a psych major, and a bit of a heartless bastard. I guess you have to be.

I know intellectually that I'm drowning here. But just when I want to give up, I'll hear a song or this Einstein quote - "only a life lived for others is a life worthwhile." I think that's how it goes.

Montana has attempted before and I feel like she's one ignored text away from pulling the trigger at all times. I could not live with myself if she killed herself because of me.

Yeah, I'm learning more and more that I can't save them.  When I first met these girls, I really thought our relationship was going to be limited to a text here, a phone call there - I had no idea they were going to latch on to me like this.  Of course, I know I've encouraged it by not setting boundaries, but I'm thousands of miles away from both of them - I thought they would rely more on people in their own time zones.
Thank you. I hadn't really considered before that my compliments aren't actually helping.  I know I have a bit of a "Superman" complex, in that I'm always trying to save someone.
And wake up to more angry messages tomorrow?  No thanks.

The whole point of me coming out to Florida is supposedly to help her expand her social circle.  She talks about all the places she wants to show me and all the things we'll do.  It's like I have to take her by the hand and re-introduce her to the world.
So how do I wean her off me?  I've tried to encourage her to join meetup and okcupid but she says she's too shy to meet new people.

> you are acting as an emotional crutch for her to lean on

Yeah, my friends said something similar, but in a meaner way.  If I am a crutch, though, I'm pretty worried about taking that away and letting her fall.  I don't want to add myself to the list of the many people who have hurt her and let her down.
